data.one_liner: Check if Android Data Saver or iOS Low Data Mode is enabled.
data.what_it_does: The plugin queries the operating system to determine the current data‑saver state. It returns enabled, whitelisted (Android only), or disabled without throwing on unsupported platforms.
use_when: You need to respect user’s low‑data preferences before heavy network calls
You want a simple way to detect Data Saver on Android or Low Data Mode on iOS/macOS
avoid_when: You require fine‑grained network type detection (Wi‑Fi vs cellular)
You need a full connectivity suite beyond data‑saver status
strengths: Supports Android, iOS, macOS and Web
weaknesses: Only reports data‑saver state, no other network info
Requires Swift Package Manager for iOS/macOS, no CocoaPods
data.setup_notes: Add the package, ensure iOS/macOS Swift Package Manager integration (Flutter 3.44+), Android minSdk 24, no extra permissions required

alternatives.name: connectivity_plus
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides broader network connectivity information, including Wi‑Fi/cellular status, though it doesn't expose data‑saver state

data.minimal_example:
const dataSaver = DataSaver();
final mode = await dataSaver.checkMode();
